text: Ketchup, pickles, cereal, sock. Ymamot Creation!
where: Ymamot Creation: little Amy in the flashback (Grace's voice)
script: [gleeful six-year-old announcing a recipe, bossy and proud, quick; Ymamot is said YAH-mah-mott] Ketchup, pickles, cereal, sock. [beat] Ymamot Creation!

text: Heading out? I can come. I have a tool belt, a flashlight and a strong opinion about whatever you're about to fight.
where: Justin offers to join the party (Gregori house talk)
script: [easygoing, friendly, goofy proud dad] Heading out? I can come. I have a tool belt, a flashlight and a strong opinion about whatever you're about to fight.

text: Great. Let me grab my jacket. And the ladder. Don't ask about the ladder.
script: [warm, cheerful, a little distracted] Great. Let me grab my jacket. And the ladder. Don't ask about the ladder.

text: No problem. The hallway light won't finish itself. It's been almost done since June.
where: Justin when Tom says not right now
script: [easygoing, dry, a little rueful] No problem. The hallway light won't finish itself. It's been almost done since June.

text: Somebody has to tag out. I'll wait. I'll be on the ladder.
where: Justin when the party is full and Tom must swap someone out
script: [easygoing, relaxed, amused] Somebody has to tag out. I'll wait. I'll be on the ladder.

text: Halftime. I have a minute. Let's go.
script: [warm, easygoing dad, a little distracted, still half watching a game] Halftime. I have a minute. Let's go.

text: Hold this. No, the other end.
script: [mildly impatient, hands full, friendly] Hold this. No, the other end.

text: Loose wire. Not my problem any more.
script: [dry, deadpan, tossing it over his shoulder] Loose wire. Not my problem any more.

text: Wire nuts! Never have enough of these.
script: [cheerful, mid-project, rummaging in his pocket] Wire nuts! Never have enough of these.

text: ARE YOU KIDDING ME WITH THAT CALL?
script: [full-throated sports yell at the TV, rising to a roar] ARE YOU KIDDING ME WITH THAT CALL?

text: This shirt cost more than your pond.
script: [smug, smooth, a wink in the voice] This shirt cost more than your pond.

text: Demo day! Wall's coming down!
script: [gleeful, pumped, shouting over the noise] Demo day! Wall's coming down!

text: Breaker's off. Breaker's... on.
script: [calm and measured, a beat of silence in the middle, then a flip] Breaker's off. Breaker's... on.

text: Ah... ah... AH CHOOOOO!
script: [slow exaggerated build, then a huge explosive sneeze] Ah... ah... AH CHOOOOO!

text: MY FOOT! WHO TOUCHED MY FOOT?!
script: [a piercing, high-pitched scream of betrayal] MY FOOT! WHO TOUCHED MY FOOT?!

text: Drywall's up. Let it dry.
script: [satisfied tradesman, wiping his hands] Drywall's up. Let it dry.

text: Not the jacket!
script: [offended gasp, protective of the jacket] Not the jacket!

text: Somebody turn the game back on.
script: [tired, bargaining, flat] Somebody turn the game back on.

text: Tell the basement I loved it.
script: [dramatic and fading, a little wry] Tell the basement I loved it.

text: And THAT is how you close out a game.
script: [triumphant sports-announcer swagger, fist pump] And THAT is how you close out a game.
